testimonials.name: Tony Yang
testimonials.title: Worship Pastor
testimonials.text: [This team] has been our go-to team for sound, lighting, and projection. From fixing problems another company left behind to guiding us through a full new building install, they’ve always gone above and beyond—training our team, answering calls even on Sundays, and standing by their work. Great company, great values, great guys!

testimonials.name: Jerry Allen
testimonials.title: Tech Director
testimonials.text: I didn’t even know what to ask at first, but [the team] was so patient and walked me step by step through the process of installing a complete AVL system in our building after it was rebuilt from tornado damage. They were understanding, trustworthy, and respectful the whole way through. Today, we have an amazing AVL system that goes far beyond my expectations.

states.name: Georgia
states.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Georgia | United Under God
states.description: Sound, livestream, lighting, and LED for Georgia churches, starting in South Georgia. See 19 Georgia churches the installation team has served.
states.h1: Church sound, video & lighting for Georgia churches
states.lead: United Under God is based in Vidalia, in the middle of South Georgia, so this is where the list starts: Savannah, Brunswick, Albany, Columbus, Vidalia, and Augusta all have churches the installation team has served. The rest of Georgia follows, from middle Georgia to metro Atlanta and the north Georgia hills.

faq.q: Do you work with churches in South Georgia?
faq.a: Yes. Churches the installation team has served in South Georgia include Compassion Church Savannah, FBC Brunswick, Byne Memorial Baptist in Albany, Christ Community Columbus, and New Life Church Vidalia. United Under God itself is based in Vidalia.

faq.q: Our church is small. Is this only for big rooms?
faq.a: No. Whether you need one microphone that finally works or a full system for a new building, the request is the same. Level Grove’s relationship with the installation team began with a single blown-speaker repair.

states.name: Florida
states.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Florida | United Under God
states.description: Church sound, livestream, lighting, and big screens for Florida churches, from Jacksonville and Tallahassee to Orlando, Tampa Bay, and Port Charlotte.
states.h1: Church sound, video & lighting for Florida churches
states.lead: The installation team’s Florida work runs from Jacksonville, St. Augustine, and Tallahassee in the north, through The Villages, Winter Park, and Odessa in central Florida, down to Port Charlotte. Many Florida churches also sit within reach of its South Georgia projects.

faq.q: Has the installation team worked in Florida?
faq.a: Yes. Florida churches it has served include Impact Church in Jacksonville, Turning Point at Calvary in St. Augustine, Transformation Church in Tallahassee, New Covenant UMC in The Villages, Calvary Orlando in Winter Park, Trinity New Life in Odessa, and New Day Christian Church in Port Charlotte.

faq.q: Our building is being rebuilt after storm damage. When should we talk about AV?
faq.a: Before the walls and ceilings are finished, so what hangs from the ceiling, the power, and the wiring are all in the plans. Unity Baptist in Newnan, Georgia was rebuilt after a tornado with all-new sound, video, lighting, and livestream.

states.name: South Carolina
states.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in South Carolina | United Under God
states.description: Church sound, livestream, lighting, and LED for South Carolina churches, from Greenville and the Upstate to Columbia, Aiken, and the coast. Send a request.
states.h1: Church sound, video & lighting for South Carolina churches
states.lead: Most of the installation team’s South Carolina work is in the Upstate (Greenville, Greer, Mauldin, and Chesnee), with more in Batesburg and Aiken. Churches on the coast are closest to its Savannah project, and we say so plainly on those pages.

faq.q: Which South Carolina churches has the installation team served?
faq.a: Calvary Chapel Baptist Greenville, Praise Cathedral Church of God in Greer, Abundant Life Church of God in Mauldin, Foster’s Grove Baptist Church in Chesnee, Samaria Baptist Church in Batesburg, and New Covenant Presbyterian Church in Aiken.

faq.q: We are on the coast. Is that too far?
faq.a: Send the request and we will tell you honestly. The nearest completed project to Charleston, Beaufort, and Hilton Head is Compassion Church Savannah.

cities.name: Savannah
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Savannah, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and lighting for Savannah, GA, from a team that has served a Savannah church. Clear speech in historic and new rooms alike.
cities.intro: Georgia’s oldest city keeps historic sanctuaries a few blocks from congregations meeting in new buildings and converted spaces. Those rooms fail in different ways: the old ones echo, the new ones are often built for music and not for speech. Compassion Church Savannah is on the installation team’s project list, so Savannah is familiar ground.

situations.text: A tall, hard sanctuary where the sermon blurs into its own echo. Start with tuning for speech and sound panels before adding volume.
Members who moved away or cannot get downtown on Sunday. A stream with steady levels that a volunteer can start the same way every week.
A newer or converted building where the band sounds fine and the spoken word does not. The system is tuned for both.

faq.q: We meet in a historic building. Can it be upgraded without changing how the room feels?
faq.a: That is a common request. Past work by the installation team includes discreet upgrades for a traditional space at Immaculate Heart of Mary in Atlanta: consistent microphones, natural lighting, and a livestream that respects the room. Tell us what must stay untouched and it becomes part of the plan.

cities.name: Brunswick
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Brunswick, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, projection, and lighting for Brunswick and the Golden Isles, from a team that has served FBC Brunswick. Tell us about your sanctuary.
cities.intro: Glynn County churches range from small chapels to large downtown congregations, and many have visitors and part-year members who keep watching after they go home. FBC Brunswick is on the installation team’s project list, so this is not new territory.

situations.text: Visitors and part-year members who want to keep worshiping with you from wherever they are. A stream built for live and on-demand viewing.
Older members who say they can hear but cannot understand the sermon. Speakers placed and tuned for every pew, not just the center aisle.
Lyrics and sermon notes the back rows cannot read. Projectors chosen for how bright the room is.

faq.q: Can the sound and screens be simple enough for whoever shows up to run them?
faq.a: That is the goal. Saved settings, clear labels, and simple controls were central to Unity Baptist’s rebuild in Newnan, and training happens once everything is tested and again on site the first Sunday.

cities.name: Valdosta
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Valdosta, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and stage lighting for Valdosta, GA churches, with the nearest past projects in Albany and Tallahassee. Tell us about your room.
cities.intro: Valdosta sits between two cities on the installation team’s project list: Albany to the northwest and Tallahassee to the southwest. No Valdosta church is on that list yet, and we will not pretend otherwise. With Valdosta State in town, many congregations here run on student volunteers who change every year.

situations.text: A young congregation that expects the room to look as good as the livestream. Lighting with saved looks a first-year volunteer can bring up.
Students who go home for the summer and still want to watch. A stream that runs from a simple, repeatable routine.
A band that keeps growing and a system that was bought for a piano and a pulpit.

faq.q: Our volunteers are mostly students who change every year. How do we keep things running?
faq.a: Plan for turnover from the start: saved settings, clear labels, and simple controls (as at Unity Baptist in Newnan), training once everything is tested, and on-site help the first Sunday.

cities.name: Albany
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Albany, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and projection for Albany and southwest Georgia, from a team that has served Byne Memorial Baptist in Albany. Send us a request.
cities.intro: Byne Memorial Baptist in Albany is on the installation team’s project list, and Albany is the hub for southwest Georgia churches from Dawson to Camilla. Many of those congregations are long-established, with members who have sat in the same pew for decades and others who now watch from home.

situations.text: An older system that has been patched for years. A new sound system designed and tuned so every seat hears clearly.
Homebound members who used to get a cassette or CD. A stream that is easy for them to find and easy for you to run.
Hymn and sermon slides that are hard to read from the back. Projectors chosen, hung, and adjusted for the sanctuary.

faq.q: Can the work be done in phases?
faq.a: Yes. Installation is done in stages (wiring, equipment, testing, final check) and scheduled around services, because Sunday is always coming. The Dream phase includes initial budgets, so you can see what fits now and what can wait.

cities.name: Columbus
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Columbus, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, LED, and lighting for Columbus, GA, from a team that has served Christ Community Columbus. Systems built for volunteer turnover.
cities.intro: Christ Community Columbus is on the installation team’s project list. Columbus churches draw from both sides of the Chattahoochee, and many serve military families from the nearby Army post who move every few years, which means the person who knows the sound board may not be here next year.

situations.text: Tech volunteers who rotate out with every move. A system with labeled saved settings and written instructions, so the next person is not starting over.
Families who moved to a new duty station and still call you home. A stream for live and on-demand viewing.
A larger room where projection washes out. An LED wall placed so every seat can see it.

faq.q: How do we keep the system usable when our tech people move away?
faq.a: Write it down and make it simple. Volunteer training and written instructions were part of Lake Point Community Church’s new sanctuary in Eatonton, and every installation includes training once everything is tested and on site the first Sunday.

cities.name: Macon
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Macon, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, LED, lighting, and acoustics for Macon and middle Georgia, with past projects nearby in Eatonton, Thomaston, Milner, and Madison. Send a request.
cities.intro: Middle Georgia is where the installation team’s project list gets dense: Lake Point Community Church in Eatonton, Mountain View Baptist in Thomaston, Rock Springs in Milner, and Madison Methodist in Madison are all within reach of Macon. None of them is in Macon itself.

situations.text: A new building on the drawing board. Audio, video, and lighting designed with the architect while the building is still on paper.
A worship center refresh where the screens are the oldest thing in the room.
A sanctuary where words get lost and the microphones squeal before it gets loud enough. Sound panels first.

faq.q: We are planning a new building. When should we call?
faq.a: Early. The Design phase covers drawings of what hangs from the ceiling and the power it needs, how much heat the equipment adds for the air conditioning, and working alongside your architect and builder, which is far easier while the building is still on paper than after the walls and ceilings are finished. Lake Point in Eatonton and Lakeside in Greensboro were both new sanctuary builds.

cities.name: Statesboro
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Statesboro, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and lighting for Statesboro, GA, including youth and student rooms, with past projects in nearby Vidalia and Savannah. Get in touch.
cities.intro: Statesboro sits between two places on the installation team’s project list: New Life Church Vidalia to the west and Compassion Church Savannah to the east. Georgia Southern keeps a steady stream of students in Statesboro’s churches, and many congregations here run a second room for students or youth.

situations.text: A student or youth room that needs its own look. Dimmable stage lighting with saved looks, separate from the sanctuary.
Students who go home on breaks and families who watch together. A stream with steady levels.
A sanctuary sound system that was never tuned to the room.

faq.q: Can a youth room or second space be done separately from the sanctuary?
faq.a: Yes. Mount Vernon in Sandy Springs had new sanctuary sound and projectors, plus a separate youth room refresh with new dimmable stage lights.

cities.name: Vidalia
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Vidalia, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and lighting for Vidalia and Toombs County, from a team that has served New Life Church Vidalia. United Under God is based here.
cities.intro: Vidalia is home for United Under God, and New Life Church Vidalia is on the installation team’s project list. If you pastor in Toombs County or the counties around it, this is the closest thing to a neighbor’s word you will find.

situations.text: One microphone that cuts out, or speakers that buzz. Small fixes count, and they are often where a good system starts.
Members who are homebound or work weekends. A stream that a volunteer can start the same way every Sunday.
Room lights that are only on or off. LED room lights with separate areas and saved settings.

faq.q: We already own some equipment. Do we have to replace it all?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Central Church in Covington moved its own sound and lighting equipment into a new sanctuary and added a new mixing board, a lighting control board, and LED room lights.

cities.name: Waycross
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Waycross, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and lighting for Waycross and Ware County churches, with the nearest past projects in Brunswick, Vidalia, and Jacksonville.
cities.intro: No Waycross church is on the installation team’s project list. The nearest are FBC Brunswick, New Life Church Vidalia, and Impact Church in Jacksonville. Many churches in Ware County and the counties around it run on one or two faithful volunteers, which shapes what a good system looks like here.

situations.text: One person is the only one who knows the board. Presets and labels so more people can run Sunday.
Shut-ins and members who drive in from the county. A stream that works without a specialist.
A screen that was added later and never fit the room.

faq.q: Only one person knows how our sound board works. What do we do?
faq.a: Make the system simple enough that more people can run it: saved settings with clear labels, written instructions, and hands-on training once everything is tested and again on the first Sunday.

cities.name: Thomasville
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Thomasville, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, choir mics, livestream, and lighting for Thomasville, GA, with nearby past projects in Tallahassee and Albany. Tell us about your sanctuary.
cities.intro: Thomasville is closer to Tallahassee than to any Georgia church on the installation team’s project list: Transformation Church in Tallahassee and Byne Memorial Baptist in Albany are the nearest. Many Thomasville congregations worship in traditional sanctuaries with choirs, where the hard part is hearing the choir and the reader, not making things louder.

situations.text: A choir that disappears in the room and on the stream. Choir microphones placed and set for the choir.
A stream where the organ is loud and the prayer is a whisper. Loudness that stays even from hymn to homily.
A beautiful room that looks dark on camera. Architectural light balance instead of a concert rig.

faq.q: Our choir is hard to hear in the room and online. Is that fixable?
faq.a: Often, yes. Choir microphone voicing and stream loudness compliance were part of the upgrades at Immaculate Heart of Mary in Atlanta, a traditional space.

cities.name: Tifton
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Tifton, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, projection, and livestream for Tifton and Tift County, including fellowship halls and chapels, with past projects nearby in Albany. Reach out.
cities.intro: Tifton sits on I-75 between Macon and Valdosta, and Byne Memorial Baptist in Albany is the nearest church on the installation team’s project list. Many churches here use one building for everything, so the fellowship hall has to work for a meal on Wednesday and overflow on Sunday.

situations.text: A fellowship hall or chapel that needs screens and simple control. Projection with a control system anyone can use.
A sanctuary system that never reached the side sections.
Overflow and homebound members who need the same service.

faq.q: Can the fellowship hall share the system for meals, meetings, and overflow?
faq.a: It can be planned that way. Word of Faith in Austell got new projection and Q-SYS control for its Chapel and Fellowship Hall alongside its worship center work.

cities.name: Augusta
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Augusta, GA | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and big screens for Augusta, GA, from a team that has served Warren in Augusta and New Covenant Presbyterian across the river in Aiken.
cities.intro: Warren in Augusta is on the installation team’s project list, and so is New Covenant Presbyterian Church just across the Savannah River in Aiken. Augusta has some of the larger congregations in east Georgia, where the question is often livestreaming, big screens, and a second campus rather than a single speaker.

situations.text: A large room where faces on stage are too small to see. Cameras that put the speaker on the big screen.
A worship center that has outgrown its projectors.
A second campus or online audience that needs the same service. Cameras, recording, and livestreaming.

faq.q: We are adding a second campus. Can the systems match?
faq.a: That is how churches with several campuses usually do it: the same saved lighting looks, the same livestream setup, and headsets so the teams can talk to each other, as in Church Unlimited’s six-campus upgrades in Corpus Christi, Texas.

cities.name: Jacksonville
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Jacksonville, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, big screens, LED walls, and livestream for Jacksonville, FL, from a team that has served Impact Church in Jacksonville. Tell us about your room.
cities.intro: Impact Church in Jacksonville is on the installation team’s project list, and Turning Point at Calvary is down the coast in St. Augustine. Jacksonville is spread out, and its churches run from neighborhood congregations to large multi-service campuses where the back row is a long way from the stage.

situations.text: A wide room where the back rows cannot see faces. Cameras that put faces on the big screen, with a plan for each shot.
Projection that washes out in a bright room. An LED wall curved and placed so every seat can see it.
Several services a weekend with different volunteers. Saved settings so each service sounds the same.

faq.q: Our room is wide and the back rows can barely see the stage. What helps?
faq.a: Big screens and LED walls placed so every seat can see them. Rock Springs in Milner, Georgia, an 1,100-seat room, got a 57' × 17' curved LED wall placed so every seat can see it.

cities.name: St. Augustine
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in St. Augustine, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church cameras, big screens, livestream, and sound for St. Augustine, FL, from the team behind the big-screen video at Turning Point at Calvary in St. Augustine.
cities.intro: Turning Point at Calvary in St. Augustine is one of the installation team’s written-up case studies: big-screen video that feels clear and natural, with camera volunteers coached. In a city this old, other congregations worship in traditional rooms where the job is the opposite: upgrades you barely notice.

situations.text: Cameras that look flat or turn skin tones odd. Camera shading, a shot grid, and coaching for the operators.
Visitors who found you on a trip and keep watching from home.
A historic room that should look like itself on camera. Architectural light balance.

faq.q: We have cameras, but the picture looks flat and skin tones look off. Do we need new cameras?
faq.a: Not always. Camera shading for skin tones, a shot grid, and sync-safe video paths were the heart of the Turning Point at Calvary work, along with coaching for the people running the cameras.

cities.name: Tallahassee
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Tallahassee, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, stage lighting, LED, and livestream for Tallahassee, FL, from a team that has served Transformation Church in Tallahassee. Send a request.
cities.intro: Transformation Church in Tallahassee is on the installation team’s project list. Tallahassee churches serve a capital city full of FSU and FAMU students alongside families who have been here for generations, and the same room often has to work for both.

situations.text: Room lights that are just on or off. LED room lights with separate areas, then stage lighting with a control board.
A young congregation that expects lyrics and video they can actually see.
Students who go home for the summer and parents who watch from out of town.

faq.q: Our lighting is just the room lights. Where do we start?
faq.a: Many churches start with LED room lights with separate areas and saved settings, then add stage lighting. Central Church in Covington, Georgia got LED room lights with separate areas, dimming, and saved settings, plus a lighting control board.

cities.name: Gainesville
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Gainesville, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, acoustics, lighting, and livestream for Gainesville, FL, with the nearest past projects in The Villages, St. Augustine, and Jacksonville.
cities.intro: No Gainesville church is on the installation team’s project list. The nearest completed projects are New Covenant UMC in The Villages, Turning Point at Calvary in St. Augustine, and Impact Church in Jacksonville. University of Florida students fill many Gainesville congregations, and many worship with a full band, sometimes in a room that was never built for one.

situations.text: A good band that the room turns into mush. Sound panels placed from measurements, before buying new speakers.
Volunteers who change every semester. Presets and labels.
Students who graduate and keep watching from wherever they land.

faq.q: Our band is good, but the room turns it into mush. Is that the speakers?
faq.a: Often it is the room. Lakeside Church in Greensboro, Georgia had sound panels placed from measurements in its new sanctuary, and Mountain View Baptist in Thomaston got sound panels so it is clearer and the microphones can get louder before they squeal.

cities.name: Orlando
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Orlando, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church livestream, cameras, LED walls, and lighting for Orlando, FL, with a past project at Calvary Orlando in nearby Winter Park. Built for multi-campus churches.
cities.intro: Calvary Orlando, on the installation team’s project list, meets in Winter Park, a few miles from downtown Orlando. Metro Orlando has many multi-service and multi-campus churches, where the stream is not an extra: it is a campus of its own.

situations.text: A stream that has failed at the worst moment. Redundant record and stream paths.
Several campuses that need the same service and the same look. The same livestream setup everywhere, and headsets so the teams can talk.
Lighting that looks different every weekend. The same saved looks every weekend.

faq.q: Our stream has failed at the worst moment. How do you make it reliable?
faq.a: Build in a backup for the recording and livestream. Church Unlimited’s six-campus work in Corpus Christi, Texas included a backup path so one failure does not take the service off the air.

cities.name: Tampa
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Tampa, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church LED walls, projection, sound, and livestream for Tampa Bay churches, with a past project at Trinity New Life in nearby Odessa. Tell us about your room.
cities.intro: Trinity New Life in Odessa, in the northern part of Tampa Bay, is on the installation team’s project list. No church in Tampa itself is. A common question here, as anywhere: keep the projectors or move to an LED wall.

situations.text: Projectors that cannot keep up with the room’s light. An LED wall sized and adjusted for the room.
A budget that does not fit an LED wall yet. Better projection now, planned so LED can follow.
A new building where everything is designed together, from the room to the stream.

faq.q: Is an LED wall better than projectors for us?
faq.a: It depends on the room’s light, size, and budget, which is why the Dream phase includes 3D renderings of design choices and initial budgets. Past work includes both: a 57' × 17' curved LED wall at Rock Springs and new projection at Mount Vernon and Lake Point.

cities.name: The Villages
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in The Villages, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Clear church sound, livestream, and readable screens for The Villages and Ocala, from a team that has served New Covenant UMC in The Villages. Reach out.
cities.intro: New Covenant UMC in The Villages is on the installation team’s project list. Churches here and in nearby Ocala serve many retirees and part-year residents, so the first goal is usually simple: every word understood, in the room and from up north.

situations.text: Members who hear the sermon but cannot make out the words. Speakers placed and tuned for clear speech in every seat.
Part-year members who worship from home in the summer. Live and on-demand viewing with even loudness.
Hymn words that are too small to read. Projectors set up for the room.

faq.q: Many members are part-time residents. Can they worship with us from up north?
faq.a: Yes, with a stream built for it: a livestream and recording for watching live or later (as at Unity Baptist in Newnan, Georgia) and loudness that stays even from hymn to sermon (as at Immaculate Heart of Mary in Atlanta).

cities.name: Port Charlotte
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Port Charlotte, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, video, and lighting for Port Charlotte, Punta Gorda, and Fort Myers, from a team that has served New Day Christian Church in Port Charlotte.
cities.intro: New Day Christian Church in Port Charlotte is on the installation team’s project list, the furthest south of its Florida work. Churches from Punta Gorda to Fort Myers are welcome to send a request. Some congregations on this coast are still repairing or rebuilding after storms, and that is the moment to plan audio, video, and lighting.

situations.text: A building being repaired or rebuilt after storm damage. A full system planned before the walls and ceilings are finished.
Existing equipment that survived and can be reused. Moved and set up again where it makes sense.
Members who are displaced or away for the season and still want to worship with you.

faq.q: Our building was damaged in a storm and is being rebuilt. When should AV be planned?
faq.a: Before the walls and ceilings are finished. Unity Baptist in Newnan, Georgia was rebuilt after a tornado with all-new sound, video, lighting, and livestream. Its tech director describes that process in his own words on this page.

cities.name: Daytona Beach
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Daytona Beach, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, LED lighting, big screens, and livestream for Daytona Beach and Volusia County, with past projects nearby in St. Augustine and Winter Park.
cities.intro: Daytona Beach sits between two cities on the installation team’s project list: St. Augustine to the north and Winter Park, beside Orlando, to the southwest. No Daytona Beach church is on the list yet.

situations.text: Old, hot stage lights. Stage lights upgraded to LED, with the extra heat planned for the air conditioning.
Visitors who watch before they ever walk in. Cameras and a stream that look like the room.
Screens that are too small for the room.

faq.q: Our stage lighting is old halogen. Is moving to LED worth it?
faq.a: Mountain View Baptist in Thomaston, Georgia upgraded its stage lights to LED with refreshed looks. The Design phase also works out how much heat the equipment adds, so the air conditioning is planned for it rather than surprised by it.

cities.name: Lakeland
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Lakeland, FL | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, projection, and audio for every room in Lakeland and Polk County, with past projects nearby in Odessa and Winter Park. Tell us about your room.
cities.intro: Lakeland sits between Tampa and Orlando, and the nearest churches on the installation team’s project list are on either side: Trinity New Life in Odessa and Calvary Orlando in Winter Park. Polk County churches often have a campus of rooms, and the service needs to reach all of them.

situations.text: A lobby, nursery, and classrooms that cannot hear the service. Sound and video carried to those rooms.
A new sanctuary that needs projectors chosen and hung before the ceiling goes up.
Lighting with saved looks, so the same volunteers can run it every week.

faq.q: Can the service be heard in the lobby, nursery, and classrooms?
faq.a: Yes. Carrying the service to the lobbies and classrooms was part of Lake Point Community Church’s new sanctuary in Eatonton, Georgia.

cities.name: Greenville
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Greenville, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and lighting for Greenville, SC, from a team that has served Calvary Chapel Baptist Greenville and churches in Mauldin and Greer.
cities.intro: The Upstate has the densest cluster of the installation team’s South Carolina work: Calvary Chapel Baptist Greenville, Abundant Life Church of God in Mauldin, and Praise Cathedral Church of God in Greer. Many Greenville churches are growing and deciding whether to upgrade the room they have or wait for the next building.

situations.text: A growing congregation where the back of the room needs the speaker on a big screen and the livestream needs to look like the room.
A worship center refresh built around an LED wall.
A new building where sound, video, LED walls, lighting, and livestream are planned together.

faq.q: We are outgrowing our room. Should we upgrade now or wait for the new building?
faq.a: Talk before deciding. Central Church in Covington, Georgia moved its existing audio and lighting into a new sanctuary instead of starting over, and Level Grove’s relationship began with a speaker repair years before its new 900-seat worship center.

cities.name: Greer
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Greer, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, lighting, and LED walls for Greer, SC, from a team that has served Praise Cathedral Church of God in Greer. Tell us about your sanctuary.
cities.intro: Praise Cathedral Church of God in Greer is on the installation team’s project list, with Greenville and Mauldin a short drive away. In churches with a full band and choir, the hardest problem is often on the platform: singers and musicians who cannot hear themselves.

situations.text: Singers and choir who cannot hear themselves. Stage and choir monitoring designed as its own system.
Lighting that should move with the worship. Stage lighting with a control board and saved looks.
Lyrics the whole choir can read. A screen facing the platform so the choir can read the words.

faq.q: Our singers and choir cannot hear themselves. What fixes that?
faq.a: Helping the choir and the band hear themselves is its own design problem. Word of Faith in Austell, Georgia got new speakers on the stage and for the choir, plus a screen facing the choir so they can read the words.

cities.name: Spartanburg
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Spartanburg, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound repair, upgrades, lighting, and livestream for Spartanburg, SC, with past projects nearby in Chesnee and Greer. Small fixes are welcome too.
cities.intro: Foster’s Grove Baptist Church in Chesnee, north of Spartanburg, and Praise Cathedral Church of God in Greer are both on the installation team’s project list. No Spartanburg church is on it yet. Many churches in the county are small, and a first call is often about one thing that broke.

situations.text: A blown speaker or a board that finally quit. Repairs count, and they are how long relationships start.
Members across the county who cannot always make it in.
A new or rebuilt sanctuary where existing equipment can be moved and set up again.

faq.q: Something just broke. Is a repair too small to ask about?
faq.a: No. Level Grove’s relationship with the installation team began with a single blown-speaker repair and grew through years of repairs, replacements, and upgrades.

cities.name: Anderson
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Anderson, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church projection, sound, and livestream for Anderson, SC and the Clemson area, with past projects nearby in Mauldin, Greenville, and Greer.
cities.intro: Anderson sits at the edge of the Upstate cluster on the installation team’s project list: Abundant Life Church of God in Mauldin, Calvary Chapel Baptist Greenville, and Praise Cathedral Church of God in Greer. No Anderson church is on the list yet. A common problem in bright sanctuaries is projection that washes out during morning services.

situations.text: A projector that washes out during morning services. A projector chosen for how bright the room is, or an LED wall where a projector cannot keep up.
A system that sounds fine for music and muddy for preaching.
Clemson students and families who watch from out of town.

faq.q: Our projector washes out during morning services. What can we do?
faq.a: Projectors have to be chosen for how bright the room is. Past projector work includes design and setup at Cedar Point Church in Claremore, Oklahoma, and choosing, hanging, and adjusting projectors at Mount Vernon in Sandy Springs, Georgia. Where projection cannot win, an LED wall may.

cities.name: Columbia
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Columbia, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and LED walls for Columbia, SC churches and schools, with past projects nearby in Batesburg and Aiken. Send a request.
cities.intro: Samaria Baptist Church in Batesburg, west of Columbia, is the nearest church on the installation team’s project list, with New Covenant Presbyterian Church in Aiken a little further. No Columbia church is on it yet. Many churches in the Midlands run more than a sanctuary: schools, gyms, and second campuses.

situations.text: A gym or multipurpose room that doubles as a worship space. A high-output system that can handle it.
A hard, round, or concrete room. Acoustic treatment and system design together.
A growing church adding campuses. Cameras and livestreaming that can grow with you.

faq.q: We also run a school with a gym. Can that be part of the plan?
faq.a: Yes. Legacy Church’s work in Albuquerque, New Mexico covered two schools, including a four-court gym with a high-output system.

cities.name: Aiken
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Aiken, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, video, and lighting for Aiken, SC, from a team that has served New Covenant Presbyterian in Aiken and Warren in Augusta. Respectful of liturgy.
cities.intro: New Covenant Presbyterian Church in Aiken is on the installation team’s project list, and Warren in Augusta is just across the river. Many Aiken congregations follow a traditional liturgy, and the worry we hear most is that screens and lights will change the feel of worship.

situations.text: Liturgy, hymns, and readings on screen without turning the sanctuary into a stage.
A choir and a reader who both need to be heard. Choir microphones set up for the choir, and tuning that puts the spoken word first.
Members who are homebound or travel. A stream with loudness that stays even.

faq.q: We follow a traditional liturgy. Will screens and lights change the feel of worship?
faq.a: They do not have to. Madison Methodist in Madison, Georgia got visual support for liturgy, teaching, and congregational participation, and Immaculate Heart of Mary in Atlanta got discreet upgrades that respect the room.

cities.name: Rock Hill
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Rock Hill, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, LED, lighting, and acoustics for new and growing churches in Rock Hill and York County, SC, with the nearest past project in Chesnee, SC.
cities.intro: Rock Hill churches sit at the edge of the growing Charlotte metro. No Rock Hill church is on the installation team’s project list; the nearest South Carolina project is Foster’s Grove Baptist Church in Chesnee. If you are planning a building, the earlier the audio, video, and lighting are in the drawings, the better.

situations.text: A new sanctuary on the drawing board. A full set of plans with the architect and the other trades.
A new room with hard surfaces. Acoustic panel layout from measurements.
LED walls chosen, hung, and adjusted as part of the build.

faq.q: We are building. What does the installation team produce for our architect?
faq.a: The Design phase produces detailed equipment drawings, drawings of what hangs from the ceiling and the power it needs, how much heat the equipment adds for the air conditioning, and complete equipment lists, worked out with your architect and builder and ending in a full set of plans.

cities.name: Charleston
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Charleston, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, acoustics, and livestream for Charleston’s historic and new sanctuaries. The nearest past project is in Savannah, and we say so plainly.
cities.intro: No Charleston church is on the installation team’s project list. The closest are Compassion Church Savannah down the coast and New Covenant Presbyterian Church in Aiken. We would rather tell you that plainly than pretend. Many of the Holy City’s historic sanctuaries are reverberant rooms that call for upgrades that respect them.

situations.text: An echoey historic room where speech gets lost. Tuning that puts the spoken word first, and careful microphone placement.
Visitors who found you on a trip and keep watching from home. Broadcast that respects the room.
Architectural light balance so the sanctuary looks like itself on camera.

faq.q: Is Charleston too far for the installation team?
faq.a: Send the request and we will tell you honestly. The team has served congregations across Georgia and the Southeast, and its nearest finished project to Charleston is in Savannah.

cities.name: Beaufort
cities.title: Church Sound, Video & Lighting in Beaufort, SC | United Under God
cities.description: Church sound, livestream, and lighting for Beaufort, Bluffton, and Hilton Head, SC. The nearest past project is Compassion Church Savannah, across the line.
cities.intro: Beaufort, Bluffton, and Hilton Head churches are closer to Savannah than to any South Carolina project on the installation team’s list. Compassion Church Savannah is the nearest. Lowcountry congregations often include military families from the bases around Beaufort and part-year residents, so the people running Sunday change often.

situations.text: Tech volunteers who rotate out with each move. Saved settings and labels any volunteer can use.
Part-year residents who worship from home the rest of the year.
A speech-first room where the sermon must be clear for older ears.

faq.q: Our volunteers change often. How do we keep the tech team staffed?
faq.a: Make the system simple enough that a new volunteer can run it: saved settings with clear labels, written instructions, training once everything is tested, and on-site help the first Sunday.
